name: 24LC1025T-I_SN
title: 24AA1025 / 24LC1025 / 24FC1025: 1024 Kbit (128K x 8) I2C serial EEPROM
summary: A 1 Mbit serial EEPROM organised as 131,072 bytes on a two-wire I2C bus. Three versions are offered: 24AA1025 from 1.7 V, 24LC1025 from 2.5 V and 24FC1025 from 1.8 V, all to 5.5 V; the FC clocks at up to 1 MHz, the others at 400 kHz. Writes go a byte or a 128-byte page at a time with a self-timed cycle of 5 ms maximum, and the WP pin locks the whole array. Pins A0 and A1 give four addresses on one bus, 4 Mbit in all; A2 must be held at VCC. 24LC1025T-I/SN is the 2.5 V grade, industrial temperature, in the 3.90 mm SOIC on tape and reel.
key_figures: 400 kHz max at 2.5 V ≤ VCC ≤ 5.5 V; 1 MHz for 24FC1025
450 µA max at VCC = 5.5 V, SCL = 400 kHz
5 ms max (3 ms typical page write)

notes: A T after the device name is tape and reel. Temperature letter I is -40°C to +85°C, E is -40°C to +125°C. Package code P is the 300 mil plastic DIP, SM the 5.28 mm plastic SOIJ, SN the 3.90 mm plastic SOIC; all are 8-lead.
The E grade is offered for the 24LC1025 only.

pins.name: A0
pins.function: Chip select bit 0, set by the user. Compared with the A0 bit of the control byte; the part answers only on a match. Tie high or low, or drive to a firm level before the part is used.

pins.name: A1
pins.function: Chip select bit 1, set by the user, compared with the A1 bit of the control byte in the same way as A0. A0 and A1 together allow four parts on one bus.

pins.name: A2
pins.function: Fixed chip select. Wire it to VCC; with it floating or at VSS the part's behaviour is undefined.

pins.name: SDA
pins.function: Serial data, both directions: address and data in, data out. Open drain, so the line needs a pull-up to VCC, about 10 kΩ at 100 kHz and 2 kΩ at 400 kHz or 1 MHz. Data changes only while SCL is low; a change with SCL high is a Start or Stop.

pins.name: SCL
pins.function: Serial clock from the bus master; times every bit in and out.

pins.name: WP
pins.function: Write protect. At VSS writes are allowed; at VCC every write is refused and reads go on as normal. Connect it to one or the other.

pins.name: VCC
pins.function: Supply: +1.7 to 5.5 V for 24AA1025, +2.5 to 5.5 V for 24LC1025, +1.8 to 5.5 V for 24FC1025.

equations.name: Address bits across four devices
equations.expr: address = A18 A17 B0 A15...A0, with A17 = control-byte A0 and A18 = control-byte A1

where.B0: block select bit, the device's A16
where.A0, A1: chip select bits of the control byte, matching the pins

equations.note: Four devices give one contiguous 4 Mbit space; a sequential read does not cross from one device to the next.

operation.text: The part is always a slave on a two-wire bus. A master supplies SCL, decides who may use the bus and issues every Start and Stop; either side may send or receive, as the master directs.

With the bus idle both lines sit high. SDA falling while SCL is high is a Start, which must open every command; SDA rising while SCL is high is a Stop, which must close every operation. Between them SDA may change only while SCL is low, one bit per clock, and the master decides how many bytes pass.

After each byte the receiver pulls SDA low through a ninth clock that the master generates, holding it low for the whole high time of that clock and meeting setup and hold. When reading, the master ends the transfer by leaving the last byte unacknowledged; the part then lets SDA go high so the master can send Stop. During an internal write cycle the part acknowledges nothing, provided the control byte polled is the one that started the write.

The first byte after Start is the control byte: code 1010, the block bit B0 (address bit A16), chip select bits A1 and A0, then R/W (1 read, 0 write). The part acknowledges only when the code and chip select bits match its pins. Two address bytes follow for a write or address set, high byte first. The array is split by B0 into two 512 Kbit halves.

Start, a write control byte, the address high byte, the address low byte and one data byte, each acknowledged, then Stop. Stop begins the internal write cycle, after which the address counter points to the next location. With WP high the part acknowledges the whole command but writes nothing and is ready for the next command at once.

As a byte write, but the master sends up to 127 more data bytes before Stop. They are held in the 128-byte page buffer and written together after Stop; the low seven address bits step after each byte. More than 128 bytes wrap round and overwrite the first ones. A page starts at a multiple of 128; a write that runs past the end of a page wraps to that page's start rather than going on to the next, so software must keep each page write within one page. Writing fewer than 128 bytes still rewrites the whole page, which is why endurance is given per page.

WP tied to VCC protects the whole array, 00000h to 1FFFFh; tied to VSS protection is off. WP is read at the Stop of each write command, with setup TSU:WP and hold THD:WP; changing it after Stop does not affect a write cycle already started.

Because the part does not acknowledge while writing, the master can find the end of the cycle by sending Start and the write control byte (R/W = 0) straight after the Stop. No acknowledge means still busy: send Start and the control byte again. An acknowledge means done, and the next read or write can follow. The polling control byte must equal the one that began the write.
The address counter holds the last address used plus one. A read control byte is acknowledged and the byte at that address is sent; the master gives no acknowledge and sends Stop.

The master sets the address with a write control byte and the two address bytes, then sends a new Start (no Stop) and a read control byte. The part acknowledges and sends one byte; the master does not acknowledge and sends Stop. The counter then points past the byte read.

Begun as a random read, but the master acknowledges each byte and the part goes on sending the next address, until the master leaves a byte unacknowledged and sends Stop. A sequential read stays inside one half: after 0FFFFh it rolls to 00000h, and after 1FFFFh to 10000h. Reading through four devices needs eight random reads.

SCL and SDA inputs are Schmitt triggers with spike filtering, and the output edge rate is controlled to limit ground bounce. Erase and write are self-timed, with the high voltage made on chip. Factory programming is offered.
